        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        # 30s timeout: Full method list with colors takes ~20s for 200+ methods
        out=$(timeout 30s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        local timeout_exit=$?
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        
        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"

        "/usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion"
        "/etc/bash_completion"
        "/opt/homebrew/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
        "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion"
        "/usr/local/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else

                    ((word_num++))

        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call

            :
        else

        fi
    else

    fi

    {
        echo "TSCompletion raw output: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Check if TSCompletion returned a callback hint
    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        # 30s timeout: Full method list with colors takes ~20s for 200+ methods
        out=$(timeout 30s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        local timeout_exit=$?
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        
        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"

#!/bin/bash
# Web4Articles Project Environment Setup

        "/etc/bash_completion"
        "/opt/homebrew/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
        "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion"
        "/usr/local/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# Generic TSCompletion-based completion function
_web4_tscompletion() {
    local component="$1" cli="$2"
    local cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}" args=("${COMP_WORDS[@]:1}")

    local BRIGHT_CYAN='\033[1;36m'
    local WHITE='\033[0;37m'
    local BRIGHT_YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
    local GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    local RED='\033[31m'

    _web4_color_command_line() {
        local current_line="$1"

        local in_word=false current_word=""
        
        while [ $i -lt ${#current_line} ]; do
            local char="${current_line:$i:1}"
            
            if [[ "$char" == " " ]]; then
                if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    fi
                    ((word_num++))
                    current_word=""
                    in_word=false
                fi
                colored_cmd+=" "
            else
                current_word+="$char"
                in_word=true
            fi
            ((i++))
        done
        
        if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
            if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"

        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        # 30s timeout: Full method list with colors takes ~20s for 200+ methods
        # Temporarily set to 10s for testing timeout detection
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        local timeout_exit=$?
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        
        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell

    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

            if [[ "$char" == " " ]]; then
                if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    fi
                    ((word_num++))
                    current_word=""
                    in_word=false
                fi
                colored_cmd+=" "

                in_word=true
            fi

                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call
    # Suppress message on double-tab (rapid successive identical calls)
    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"
    
    # Check if this is a rapid repeat (double-tab scenario)
    if [[ "${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY:-}" == "$cache_key" ]]; then
        local time_diff=$((current_time - ${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME:-0}))
        if [ $time_diff -le 2 ]; then
            # Suppress message on double-tab within 2 seconds
            :
        else
            printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
        fi
    else
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
    fi
    
    # Cache this completion call
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY="$cache_key"
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME="$current_time"
    
    local out=$(NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --loader ts-node/esm "$tsc" "${completeArgs[@]}" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
    
    {
        echo "TSCompletion raw output: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Check if TSCompletion returned a callback hint
    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
            echo "Args array length: ${#args[@]}"
            echo "Args[0]: '${args[0]}'"
            echo "Args[1]: '${args[1]}'"
            echo "Args[2]: '${args[2]}'"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        # 30s timeout: Full method list with colors takes ~20s for 200+ methods
        # Temporarily set to 10s for testing timeout detection
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        local timeout_exit=$?
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        
        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

    # Check if TSCompletion returned a callback hint
    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
            echo "Args array length: ${#args[@]}"
            echo "Args[0]: '${args[0]}'"
            echo "Args[1]: '${args[1]}'"
            echo "Args[2]: '${args[2]}'"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        # 30s timeout: Full method list with colors takes ~20s for 200+ methods
        # Temporarily set to 10s for testing timeout detection
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        local timeout_exit=$?
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        
        # Detect timeout (exit code 124)
        if [ $timeout_exit -eq 124 ]; then
            {
                echo "⚠️  TIMEOUT: Callback exceeded 30s limit"
            } >> "$logfile"
            printf "\n${RED}⏱️  Completion timed out (>30s) - falling back to file completion${NO_COLOR}\n"
            printf "   Hint: This usually means complex completion logic needs optimization\n"
            COMPREPLY=()
            return 0
        fi
        
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"

  protected discoverMethods(): void {

    while (currentPrototype && currentPrototype !== Object.prototype) {
      const methodNames = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(currentPrototype)
        .filter(name => typeof currentPrototype[name] === 'function')
        .filter(name => !name.startsWith('_') && name !== 'constructor')
        .filter(name => !['init', 'toScenario', 'validateModel', 'getModel'].includes(name));

      for (const methodName of methodNames) {
        // Don't overwrite if already discovered (subclass takes precedence)
        if (!this.methodSignatures.has(methodName)) {
          const method = currentPrototype[methodName];
          this.methodSignatures.set(methodName, {
            name: methodName,
            paramCount: method.length,
            isAsync: method.constructor.name === 'AsyncFunction'
          });
        }
      }
      
      // Move up the chain
      currentPrototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(currentPrototype);
    }
    
    // Also discover component methods if componentClass is set

      const prototype = this.componentClass.prototype;
      const methodNames = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(prototype)
        .filter(name => typeof prototype[name] === 'function')
        .filter(name => !name.startsWith('_') && name !== 'constructor')
        .filter(name => !['init', 'toScenario', 'validateModel', 'getModel'].includes(name));

      for (const methodName of methodNames) {

        this.methodSignatures.set(methodName, {
          name: methodName,
          paramCount: method.length,
          isAsync: method.constructor.name === 'AsyncFunction'
        });
      }
    }

  /**

  protected async executeDynamicCommand(command: string, args: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!this.methodSignatures.has(command)) {
      return false; // Command not found
    }

    const signature = this.methodSignatures.get(command)!;
    
    // Dynamic argument validation with overload support
    const minArgs = this.getMinimumArguments(command);
    if (args.length < minArgs) {
      throw new Error(`At least ${minArgs} arguments required for ${command} command`);
    }

    // Check if method exists on CLI (this) or component
    // CLI methods take precedence (e.g., completeParameter, actionParameterCompletion)
    if (typeof (this as any)[command] === 'function') {
      // Execute on CLI instance (DefaultCLI or Web4TSComponentCLI)
      const method = (this as any)[command];
      if (signature.isAsync) {
        await method.apply(this, args);
      } else {
        method.apply(this, args);
      }
    } else {
      // Fallback to component instance
      const componentInstance = this.getComponentInstance();
      const method = componentInstance[command];
      
      if (signature.isAsync) {
        await method.apply(componentInstance, args);
      } else {
        method.apply(componentInstance, args);
      }
    }
    
    return true;
  }

    // Dynamic usage generation from discovered methods

  /**

   */
  protected analyzeComponentMethods(): MethodInfo[] {
    if (!this.componentClass) return [];
    
    const methods: MethodInfo[] = [];
    const prototype = this.componentClass.prototype;
    const methodNames = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(prototype);
    
    // Whitelist for internal CLI methods that start with __ (hidden but executable)
    const internalCLIMethods = ['__completeParameter'];
    
    for (const name of methodNames) {
      // Skip constructor and private methods (except whitelisted internal CLI methods)
      if (name === 'constructor') continue;
      if (name.startsWith('_') && !internalCLIMethods.includes(name)) continue;
      
      // ✅ ZERO CONFIG: Check @cliHide annotation with enhanced processing
      const cliAnnotations = TSCompletion.extractCliAnnotations(this.componentClass.name, name);
      if (cliAnnotations.hide) {
        continue;
      }
      
      const method = prototype[name];
      if (typeof method === 'function') {
        methods.push({
          name: name,
          parameters: this.extractParameterInfoFromTSCompletion(name),
          description: this.extractMethodDescriptionFromTSDoc(name),
          examples: this.extractExamplesFromTSDoc(name),
          returnType: 'any',
          isPublic: !name.startsWith('_'),
          category: this.categorizeMethod(name)
        });
      }
    }
    
    return methods;
  }

  /**
   * Extract method description from TSDoc annotations
   */
  private extractMethodDescriptionFromTSDoc(methodName: string): string {
    try {
      // Try to extract description from TSCompletion
      const componentInstance = this.getComponentInstance();
      if (componentInstance) {
        const componentClassName = componentInstance.constructor.name;
        // Get full method documentation using TSCompletion
        const fullMethodDoc = TSCompletion.getMethodDoc(componentClassName, methodName);
        
        if (fullMethodDoc) {
          // Extract first meaningful line from TSDoc
          const lines = fullMethodDoc.split('\n');
          for (const line of lines) {
            const cleaned = line.replace(/^\s*\*\s*/, '').trim();
            if (cleaned && !cleaned.startsWith('@') && cleaned !== '/**' && cleaned !== '*/') {
              return cleaned;
            }
          }
        }
      }
    } catch (error) {
      // Continue to fallback
    }
    
    // If TSDoc extraction failed, return method name only (no fallback descriptions)
    return methodName;
  }

  /**
   * Extract examples from TSDoc @example annotations
   */
  private extractExamplesFromTSDoc(methodName: string): string[] {
    try {
      const componentInstance = this.getComponentInstance();
      if (componentInstance) {
        const componentClassName = componentInstance.constructor.name;
        
        // Get full method documentation using TSCompletion
        const fullMethodDoc = TSCompletion.getMethodDoc(componentClassName, methodName);
        
        if (fullMethodDoc) {
          const examples: string[] = [];
          const lines = fullMethodDoc.split('\n');
          let inExampleSection = false;
          
          for (const line of lines) {
            const cleaned = line.replace(/^\s*\*\s*/, '').trim();
            
            if (cleaned.startsWith('@example')) {
              inExampleSection = true;
              const exampleText = cleaned.replace('@example', '').trim();
              if (exampleText) {
                examples.push(exampleText);
              }
            } else if (inExampleSection && cleaned && !cleaned.startsWith('@')) {
              examples.push(cleaned);
            } else if (cleaned.startsWith('@') && !cleaned.startsWith('@example')) {
              inExampleSection = false;
            }
          }
          
          if (examples.length > 0) {
            return examples;
          }
        }
      }
    } catch (error) {
      // Continue to fallback
    }
    
    // If no TSDoc examples found, return method name only
    return [methodName];
  }

  /**
