```plaintext
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$logfile")" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Color definitions for OOSH-style command line display (DRY - defined once)
    # Use DefaultCLI color scheme: [1;36m=command, [0;37m=method, [1;33m=parameters
    local BRIGHT_CYAN='\033[1;36m'
    local WHITE='\033[0;37m'
    local BRIGHT_YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
    local GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    local RED='\033[31m'
    local NO_COLOR='\033[0m'
    
    # Helper function: Apply colors to command line (DRY - reused by both completion paths)
    _web4_color_command_line() {
        local current_line="$1"
        local colored_cmd=""
        local i=0 word_num=0
        local in_word=false current_word=""
        
        while [ $i -lt ${#current_line} ]; do
            local char="${current_line:$i:1}"
            
            if [[ "$char" == " " ]]; then
                if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    fi
                    ((word_num++))
                    current_word=""
                    in_word=false
                fi
                colored_cmd+=" "
            else
                current_word+="$char"
                in_word=true
            fi
            ((i++))
        done
        
        if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
            if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            else
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            fi
        fi
        
        echo "$colored_cmd"
    }
    
    # Debug logging
    {
        echo "=== $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ==="
        echo "Component: $component"
        echo "CLI: $cli"
        echo "Current word (cur): '$cur'"
        echo "COMP_CWORD: $COMP_CWORD"
        echo "COMP_WORDS: ${COMP_WORDS[*]}"
        echo "Args (after CLI): ${args[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile" 2>&1
    
    [ ! -f "$tsc" ] && {
        echo "ERROR: TSCompletion not found at $tsc" >> "$logfile"
        return 0
    }
    
    # INJECT class name as first arg for TSCompletion
    # TSCompletion expects: [className, methodName, ...params]
    # Use comma-separated list (Web4 standard) to get BOTH CLI and component methods
    # User types: web4tscomponent links <Tab>
    # We inject: Web4TSComponentCLI,DefaultWeb4TSComponent links <Tab>
    # TSCompletion scans CLI extends hierarchy: Web4TSComponentCLI → DefaultCLI (auto-discovered)
    local className="${component}CLI,Default${component}"
    
    # OOSH UX Pattern: Auto-trigger hierarchical method display when no method specified
    # web4tscomponent <TAB> → Direct callback to get numbered list with parameters
    # web4tscomponent com<TAB> → Filtered hierarchical list (only methods starting with 'com')
    # Bypasses TSCompletion ambiguity, goes straight to hierarchical display
    local completeArgs
    if [ ${#args[@]} -eq 0 ] || ([ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${args[0]}" != "" ]); then
        # No args OR single partial method name → hierarchical display with optional filter
        local filter="${args[0]:-}"
        
        {
            echo "Auto-injected hierarchical display callback with filter: '$filter'"
            echo "Callback: completionNameParameterCompletion completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # Process callback immediately
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for callback execution
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${filter}\`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method ${filter}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        out=$($cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "$filter" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # Multi-line completion: show hierarchical display
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Extract tokens for COMPREPLY
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)
            # Output format: "methodName <params>\n────\n📖 Documentation:\n..."
            # Extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
                # No numbered entries found - likely single match with TSDoc
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                # Strip ANSI codes and extract first word
                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            # This allows bash to complete "compl" → "completion " and move to next parameter
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                # Extract method name from first line (strip ANSI codes and parameters)
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    # Strip ANSI codes
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    # Extract just method name (before first space or parameter marker)
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Multiple matches or extraction failed: Use method names for bash completion
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                # Use actual method names for COMPREPLY, not numbers
                # bash will filter them based on current word
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                # No tokens extracted → empty output, prevent fallback
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        else
            # Fallback to standard completion
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
            return 0
        fi
    elif [ "${args[0]}" = "" ]; then
        # Empty first arg (just space after command) → hierarchical display
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli \`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method \`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        out=$($cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
        
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call
    # Suppress message on double-tab (rapid successive identical calls)
    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"
    
    # Check if this is a rapid repeat (double-tab scenario)
    if [[ "${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY:-}" == "$cache_key" ]]; then
        local time_diff=$((current_time - ${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME:-0}))
        if [ $time_diff -le 2 ]; then
            # Suppress message on double-tab within 2 seconds
            :
        else
            printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
        fi
    else
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
    fi
    
    # Cache this completion call
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY="$cache_key"
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME="$current_time"
    
    local out=$(NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --loader ts-node/esm "$tsc" "${completeArgs[@]}" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
    
    {
        echo "TSCompletion raw output: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Check if TSCompletion returned a callback hint
    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"
```

```plaintext
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')

                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Multiple matches or extraction failed: Use method names for bash completion
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                # Use actual method names for COMPREPLY, not numbers
                # bash will filter them based on current word
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                # No tokens extracted → empty output, prevent fallback
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        else
            # Fallback to standard completion
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
            return 0
        fi
    elif [ "${args[0]}" = "" ]; then
        # Empty first arg (just space after command) → hierarchical display
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli \`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method \`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        out=$(timeout 5s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
        
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"

            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')

                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')

                    fi
                fi

                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi

                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"

    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"
    
    # Check if this is a rapid repeat (double-tab scenario)
    if [[ "${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY:-}" == "$cache_key" ]]; then
        local time_diff=$((current_time - ${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME:-0}))
        if [ $time_diff -le 2 ]; then
            # Suppress message on double-tab within 2 seconds
            :
        else

        fi

    fi
    
    # Cache this completion call
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY="$cache_key"
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME="$current_time"
    
    local out=$(NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --loader ts-node/esm "$tsc" "${completeArgs[@]}" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
    
    {
        echo "TSCompletion raw output: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Check if TSCompletion returned a callback hint
    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"
```

```plaintext
        "/opt/homebrew/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
        "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion"
        "/usr/local/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

            local char="${current_line:$i:1}"

                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else

                    ((word_num++))

                    in_word=false

                colored_cmd+=" "
            else
                current_word+="$char"
                in_word=true
            fi
            ((i++))

        if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
            if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then

            elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then

            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}
```

```plaintext
#!/bin/bash
# Web4Articles Project Environment Setup

# TypeScript-first approach: Minimal shell, maximum TypeScript

# Load bash-completion framework if available
_web4_load_bash_completion() {
    type _init_completion &>/dev/null && return 0
    local paths=(
        "/usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion"
        "/etc/bash_completion"
        "/opt/homebrew/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
        "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion"
        "/usr/local/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# Generic TSCompletion-based completion function
_web4_tscompletion() {
    local component="$1" cli="$2"
    local cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}" args=("${COMP_WORDS[@]:1}")
    
    # CRITICAL: Bash drops trailing empty elements from arrays
    # If cur is empty (user typed space after last word), we need to preserve it
    # Example: "web4tscomponent completion method <TAB>" → args should be ("completion" "method" "")
    # But ONLY if args is not empty - don't turn empty args into args with one empty element!
    if [ -z "$cur" ] && [ ${#args[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ $((COMP_CWORD - 1)) -gt ${#args[@]} ]; then
        args+=("")  # Add explicit empty element
    fi
    
    local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$component/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
    local logfile="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/temp/logs/completion-debug.log"

    # Ensure our log directory exists (source.env owns this requirement)
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$logfile")" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Color definitions for OOSH-style command line display (DRY - defined once)
    # Use DefaultCLI color scheme: [1;36m=command, [0;37m=method, [1;33m=parameters
    local BRIGHT_CYAN='\033[1;36m'
    local WHITE='\033[0;37m'
    local BRIGHT_YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
    local GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    local RED='\033[31m'
    local NO_COLOR='\033[0m'
    
    # Helper function: Apply colors to command line (DRY - reused by both completion paths)
    _web4_color_command_line() {
        local current_line="$1"
        local colored_cmd=""
        local i=0 word_num=0
        local in_word=false current_word=""
        
        while [ $i -lt ${#current_line} ]; do
            local char="${current_line:$i:1}"
            
            if [[ "$char" == " " ]]; then
                if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    fi
                    ((word_num++))
                    current_word=""
                    in_word=false
                fi
                colored_cmd+=" "
            else
                current_word+="$char"
                in_word=true
            fi
            ((i++))
        done
        
        if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
            if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            else
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            fi
        fi
        
        echo "$colored_cmd"
    }
    
    # Debug logging
    {
        echo "=== $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ==="
        echo "Component: $component"
        echo "CLI: $cli"
        echo "Current word (cur): '$cur'"
        echo "COMP_CWORD: $COMP_CWORD"
        echo "COMP_WORDS: ${COMP_WORDS[*]}"
        echo "Args (after CLI): ${args[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile" 2>&1
    
    [ ! -f "$tsc" ] && {

        return 0
    }

    # TSCompletion expects: [className, methodName, ...params]
    # Use comma-separated list (Web4 standard) to get BOTH CLI and component methods
    # User types: web4tscomponent links <Tab>
    # We inject: Web4TSComponentCLI,DefaultWeb4TSComponent links <Tab>
    # TSCompletion scans CLI extends hierarchy: Web4TSComponentCLI → DefaultCLI (auto-discovered)
    local className="${component}CLI,Default${component}"

    # web4tscomponent <TAB> → Direct callback to get numbered list with parameters
    # web4tscomponent com<TAB> → Filtered hierarchical list (only methods starting with 'com')
    # Bypasses TSCompletion ambiguity, goes straight to hierarchical display
    local completeArgs
    if [ ${#args[@]} -eq 0 ] || ([ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${args[0]}" != "" ]); then
        # No args OR single partial method name → hierarchical display with optional filter
        local filter="${args[0]:-}"
        
        {
            echo "Auto-injected hierarchical display callback with filter: '$filter'"
            echo "Callback: completionNameParameterCompletion completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"

        } >> "$logfile"

                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")

                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"

                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then

                    fi

            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)

                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then

                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            # This allows bash to complete "compl" → "completion " and move to next parameter
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                # Extract method name from first line (strip ANSI codes and parameters)
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)

                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

        {

        } >> "$logfile"

        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"
```

```plaintext
    # User types: web4tscomponent links <Tab>
    # We inject: Web4TSComponentCLI,DefaultWeb4TSComponent links <Tab>
    # TSCompletion scans CLI extends hierarchy: Web4TSComponentCLI → DefaultCLI (auto-discovered)
    local className="${component}CLI,Default${component}"
    
    # OOSH UX Pattern: Auto-trigger hierarchical method display when no method specified
    # web4tscomponent <TAB> → Direct callback to get numbered list with parameters
    # web4tscomponent com<TAB> → Filtered hierarchical list (only methods starting with 'com')
    # Bypasses TSCompletion ambiguity, goes straight to hierarchical display
    local completeArgs
    if [ ${#args[@]} -eq 0 ] || ([ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${args[0]}" != "" ]); then
        # No args OR single partial method name → hierarchical display with optional filter

        {
            echo "Auto-injected hierarchical display callback with filter: '$filter'"
            echo "Callback: completionNameParameterCompletion completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # Process callback immediately
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for callback execution

        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method ${filter}\`\n"

            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Extract tokens for COMPREPLY
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)

                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            # This allows bash to complete "compl" → "completion " and move to next parameter
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                # Extract method name from first line (strip ANSI codes and parameters)
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"

                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')

                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Multiple matches or extraction failed: Use method names for bash completion
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                # Use actual method names for COMPREPLY, not numbers
                # bash will filter them based on current word
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                # No tokens extracted → empty output, prevent fallback
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        else
            # Fallback to standard completion
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
            return 0
        fi
    elif [ "${args[0]}" = "" ]; then

        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli \`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method \`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        out=$($cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "" 2>>"$logfile" || true)

            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"

                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")

                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi

                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi

                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call
    # Suppress message on double-tab (rapid successive identical calls)
    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"
    
    # Check if this is a rapid repeat (double-tab scenario)
    if [[ "${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY:-}" == "$cache_key" ]]; then
        local time_diff=$((current_time - ${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME:-0}))
        if [ $time_diff -le 2 ]; then
            # Suppress message on double-tab within 2 seconds
            :
        else
            printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"

    } >> "$logfile"

    if [[ "$out" == __CALLBACK__:* ]]; then
        local callback="${out#__CALLBACK__:}"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for slow callback execution
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

# OOSH-inspired colored PS1 prompt for Web4
export PS1="\[\e[0m\][web4 \[\e[36m\]\u\[\e[0m\]@\[\e[32m\]\h\[\e[0m\]] \[\e[33;1m\]\w\[\e[0m\] > "

echo "✅ Web4 environment loaded (TypeScript-first, no ENV vars)"

# OOSH-style welcome message at the bottom (like OOSH bashrc)
echo -e "\033[36m
    🚀 Welcome to Web4 OOP Shell
    ✨ TypeScript-first development environment
    🎯 Tab completion with hierarchical display

\033[0m"
```

```plaintext
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then

                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')

                    return 0

                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')

    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call

    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"

        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"

        } >> "$logfile"

        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback ${args[*]}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Call TypeScript to execute the completion callback (Web4 pattern: @cliHide not __ prefix)
        # Pass all args (e.g., 'on Unit') so completion method has context
        # Preserve trailing newlines by adding a marker and removing it
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)
    # If output contains newlines → Multi-LINE completion (hierarchical display)
    # Otherwise → Standard single-word completion (use compgen filtering)
    if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
        {
            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"
            echo "Using printf for colored display + clean tokens for COMPREPLY"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            for i in "${!tokens[@]}"; do
                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else
        {
            echo "Single-word completion detected (standard pattern)"
            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions

\033[0m"
```

```plaintext
        # Standard Pattern: Use compgen for prefix filtering
        # Works for simple single-word completions (backward compatible)
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
        
        # Note: Spacing handled by bash completion flags, no manual addition needed
    fi
    
    {
        echo "COMPREPLY (after hybrid completion with cur='$cur'): ${COMPREPLY[*]}"
        echo "COMPREPLY count: ${#COMPREPLY[@]}"
        echo "---"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Only enable default completions (files/dirs) if we have NO custom completions
    # This prevents mixing our completion values with random files/directories
    if [ ${#COMPREPLY[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        compopt -o default 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# Auto-register completions for all CLIs
_web4_register_completions() {
    local scripts="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts" registered=()
    [ ! -d "$scripts" ] && return 0
    
    for cli in "$scripts"/*; do
        [ -x "$cli" ] && [ ! -d "$cli" ] || continue
        local name=$(basename "$cli")
        [[ "$name" =~ -v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]] && continue
        
        if [ -L "$cli" ]; then
            local target=$(readlink "$cli")
            if [[ "$target" =~ components/([^/]+)/latest ]]; then
                local comp="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$comp/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
                if [ -f "$tsc" ]; then
                    eval "_${name}_completion() { _web4_tscompletion '$comp' '$name'; }"
                    complete -F "_${name}_completion" "$name" -o nospace
                    registered+=("$name")
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    [ ${#registered[@]} -gt 0 ] && echo "🎯 Tab completion enabled for: ${registered[*]}"
}

# Initialize completions (suppress all errors from bash-completion framework)
_web4_load_bash_completion >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
_web4_register_completions
```

```plaintext
#!/bin/bash
# Web4Articles Project Environment Setup
# Version: 0.3.13.2 (MUST manually update when template changes)
# TypeScript-first approach: Minimal shell, maximum TypeScript

# Useful aliases
alias ll='ls -la'

# Project Root - Required for tab completion bootstrap
export WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"

# Add scripts to PATH
export PATH="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts:$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/versions:$PATH"

# Enable single TAB completion display
# show-all-if-ambiguous: show all completions on first TAB when multiple matches
bind 'set show-all-if-ambiguous on'

echo "🔨 Web4 scripts added to PATH"

# ============================================================================
# 🎯 Tab Completion Setup for Web4 CLIs
# ============================================================================

# Load bash-completion framework if available
_web4_load_bash_completion() {
    type _init_completion &>/dev/null && return 0
    local paths=(
        "/usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion"
        "/etc/bash_completion"
        "/opt/homebrew/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
        "/usr/local/etc/bash_completion"
        "/usr/local/etc/profile.d/bash_completion.sh"
    )
    for p in "${paths[@]}"; do
        [ -f "$p" ] && . "$p" && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# Generic TSCompletion-based completion function
_web4_tscompletion() {
    local component="$1" cli="$2"
    local cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}" args=("${COMP_WORDS[@]:1}")
    
    # CRITICAL: Bash drops trailing empty elements from arrays
    # If cur is empty (user typed space after last word), we need to preserve it
    # Example: "web4tscomponent completion method <TAB>" → args should be ("completion" "method" "")
    # But ONLY if args is not empty - don't turn empty args into args with one empty element!
    if [ -z "$cur" ] && [ ${#args[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ $((COMP_CWORD - 1)) -ge ${#args[@]} ]; then
        args+=("")  # Add explicit empty element
    fi
    
    local tsc="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/components/$component/latest/src/ts/layer4/TSCompletion.ts"
    local logfile="$WEB4_PROJECT_ROOT/temp/logs/completion-debug.log"

    # Ensure our log directory exists (source.env owns this requirement)
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$logfile")" 2>/dev/null || true
    touch "$logfile" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Color definitions for OOSH-style command line display (DRY - defined once)
    # Use DefaultCLI color scheme: [1;36m=command, [0;37m=method, [1;33m=parameters
    local BRIGHT_CYAN='\033[1;36m'
    local WHITE='\033[0;37m'
    local BRIGHT_YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
    local GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    local RED='\033[31m'
    local NO_COLOR='\033[0m'
    
    # Helper function: Apply colors to command line (DRY - reused by both completion paths)
    _web4_color_command_line() {
        local current_line="$1"
        local colored_cmd=""
        local i=0 word_num=0
        local in_word=false current_word=""
        
        while [ $i -lt ${#current_line} ]; do
            local char="${current_line:$i:1}"
            
            if [[ "$char" == " " ]]; then
                if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
                    if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                        colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    else
                        colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
                    fi
                    ((word_num++))
                    current_word=""
                    in_word=false
                fi
                colored_cmd+=" "
            else
                current_word+="$char"
                in_word=true
            fi
            ((i++))
        done
        
        if [ "$in_word" = true ]; then
            if [ $word_num -eq 0 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_CYAN}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            elif [ $word_num -eq 1 ]; then
                colored_cmd+="${WHITE}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            else
                colored_cmd+="${BRIGHT_YELLOW}${current_word}${NO_COLOR}"
            fi
        fi
        
        echo "$colored_cmd"
    }
    
    # Debug logging
    {
        echo "=== $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') ==="
        echo "Component: $component"
        echo "CLI: $cli"
        echo "Current word (cur): '$cur'"
        echo "COMP_CWORD: $COMP_CWORD"
        echo "COMP_WORDS: ${COMP_WORDS[*]}"
        echo "Args (after CLI): ${args[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile" 2>&1
    
    [ ! -f "$tsc" ] && {
        echo "ERROR: TSCompletion not found at $tsc" >> "$logfile"
        return 0
    }
    
    # INJECT class name as first arg for TSCompletion
    # TSCompletion expects: [className, methodName, ...params]
    # Use comma-separated list (Web4 standard) to get BOTH CLI and component methods
    # User types: web4tscomponent links <Tab>
    # We inject: Web4TSComponentCLI,DefaultWeb4TSComponent links <Tab>
    # TSCompletion scans CLI extends hierarchy: Web4TSComponentCLI → DefaultCLI (auto-discovered)
    local className="${component}CLI,Default${component}"
    
    # OOSH UX Pattern: Auto-trigger hierarchical method display when no method specified
    # web4tscomponent <TAB> → Direct callback to get numbered list with parameters
    # web4tscomponent com<TAB> → Filtered hierarchical list (only methods starting with 'com')
    # Bypasses TSCompletion ambiguity, goes straight to hierarchical display
    local completeArgs
    if [ ${#args[@]} -eq 0 ] || ([ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ] && [ "${args[0]}" != "" ]); then
        # No args OR single partial method name → hierarchical display with optional filter
        local filter="${args[0]:-}"
        
        {
            echo "Auto-injected hierarchical display callback with filter: '$filter'"
            echo "Callback: completionNameParameterCompletion completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # Process callback immediately
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        {
            echo "Detected callback: $callback"
            echo "Calling: $cli completeParameter $callback completion method $filter"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Immediate feedback for callback execution
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${filter}\`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method ${filter}\`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$($cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "$filter" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # Multi-line completion: show hierarchical display
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Extract tokens for COMPREPLY
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)
            # Output format: "methodName <params>\n────\n📖 Documentation:\n..."
            # Extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
                # No numbered entries found - likely single match with TSDoc
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                # Strip ANSI codes and extract first word
                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            # This allows bash to complete "compl" → "completion " and move to next parameter
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                # Extract method name from first line (strip ANSI codes and parameters)
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    # Strip ANSI codes
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    # Extract just method name (before first space or parameter marker)
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Multiple matches or extraction failed: Use method names for bash completion
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                # Use actual method names for COMPREPLY, not numbers
                # bash will filter them based on current word
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                # No tokens extracted → empty output, prevent fallback
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        else
            # Fallback to standard completion
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$out" -- "$cur") )
            return 0
        fi
    elif [ "${args[0]}" = "" ]; then
        # Empty first arg (just space after command) → hierarchical display
        local callback="completionNameParameterCompletion"
        
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli \`\n"
        printf "🎯 Executing completion callback: \`$cli completeParameter $callback completion method \`\n"
        printf "💭 Thinking...\n"
        
        out=$($cli completeParameter "$callback" "completion" "method" "" 2>>"$logfile" || true)
        
        if [[ "$out" == *$'\n'* ]]; then
            printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
            
            local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
            local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
            printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
            
            # Strip ANSI codes from entire output FIRST, then parse
            local clean_out=$(echo "$out" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
            
            local tokens=()
            local method_names=()
            while IFS= read -r line; do
                if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+):[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
                    # Extract method name (first word from cleaned line)
                    local rest="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
                    local method_name=$(echo "$rest" | awk '{print $1}')
                    if [ -n "$method_name" ]; then
                        method_names+=("$method_name")
                    fi
                fi
            done <<< "$clean_out"
            
            # Special case: Single match with documentation (no numbers)
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                local clean_method=$(echo "$first_line" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | awk '{print $1}')
                if [ -n "$clean_method" ]; then
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            # Special case: Single numbered match → extract method name and auto-complete
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -eq 1 ]; then
                local first_line=$(echo "$out" | head -1)
                if [[ "$first_line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(.+) ]]; then
                    local method_with_params="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
                    local clean_method=$(echo "$method_with_params" | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
                    clean_method=$(echo "$clean_method" | awk '{print $1}')
                    COMPREPLY=("$clean_method ")
                    return 0
                fi
            fi
            
            if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ] && [ ${#method_names[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${method_names[*]}" -- "$cur") )
            else
                COMPREPLY=()
            fi
            return 0
        fi
    else
        completeArgs=("$className" "${args[@]}")
    fi
    
    {
        echo "ClassName injected: $className"
        echo "Complete args to TSCompletion: ${completeArgs[*]}"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # OOSH Pattern: Immediate user feedback before slow TypeScript call
    # Suppress message on double-tab (rapid successive identical calls)
    local cache_key="$cli:${args[*]}"
    local current_time=$(date +%s)
    local last_completion_key="${cache_key}"
    local last_completion_time="${current_time}"
    
    # Check if this is a rapid repeat (double-tab scenario)
    if [[ "${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY:-}" == "$cache_key" ]]; then
        local time_diff=$((current_time - ${_WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME:-0}))
        if [ $time_diff -le 2 ]; then
            # Suppress message on double-tab within 2 seconds
            :
        else
            printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
        fi
    else
        printf "\n🔍 Calculating completions for: \`$cli ${args[*]}\`\n"
    fi
    
    # Cache this completion call
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_KEY="$cache_key"
    export _WEB4_LAST_COMPLETION_TIME="$current_time"
    
    local out=$(NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node --loader ts-node/esm "$tsc" "${completeArgs[@]}" 2>>"$logfile" || true)

        # Use timeout to prevent infinite hangs on typos or edge cases
        out=$(timeout 10s $cli completeParameter "$callback" "${args[@]}" 2>>"$logfile"; echo "PRESERVE_NEWLINES" || true)
        out="${out%PRESERVE_NEWLINES}"
        {
            echo "Callback returned: '$out'"
        } >> "$logfile"
    fi
    
    {
        echo "Final output for compgen: '$out'"
    } >> "$logfile"
    
    # Smart Hybrid Detection (OOSH-inspired pattern)

            echo "Multi-LINE completion detected (OOSH pattern)"

        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Pattern: Show colored hierarchy to user via printf
        printf "\n%s\n" "$out"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display (like OOSH does) - NO trailing newline
        # Apply colors using DRY helper function
        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"
        local colored_cmd=$(_web4_color_command_line "$current_line")
        
        printf "\nyour ${BRIGHT_CYAN}web4${NO_COLOR} command > $colored_cmd${RED}${COMP_LINE:$COMP_POINT}${NO_COLOR}"
        
        # Extract clean tokens for COMPREPLY (look for patterns like "1a", "17b")
        local tokens=()
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            if [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+[a-z])\) ]]; then
                tokens+=("${BASH_REMATCH[1]}")
            fi
        done <<< "$out"
        
        # Add space to tokens for multi-line completions (cursor positioning)
        if [ ${#tokens[@]} -gt 0 ]; then

                tokens[i]+=" "
            done
        fi
        
        # Set COMPREPLY to prevent default completion
        COMPREPLY=("${tokens[@]}")
        return 0
        
    else

            echo "Using compgen-based filtering"
        } >> "$logfile"
        
        # OOSH Command Line Display for single-word completions too

        local current_line="${COMP_LINE:0:$COMP_POINT}"

    fi
```

# Known Bugs - 2025-10-14 Session

## 🐛 Active Bugs

### Bug 1: `web4tscomponent completion method <TAB>` Falls Back to File Listing

**Status:** 🔴 Active - Not Fixed  
**Severity:** Medium  
**Discovered:** 2025-10-19  
**Session:** 2025-10-14-UTC-0948

When user types `web4tscomponent completion method <TAB>`, the tab completion falls back to directory/file listing instead of showing the method list.

Should display numbered list of all 200+ methods (same as `web4tscomponent <TAB>`).
